newsitem.title: USA: ABC TV executive Tarses to remain.
newsitem.headline: ABC TV executive Tarses to remain.

text.p: Jamie Tarses, the embattled president of ABC Entertainment, said Wednesday said she has no plans to leave the television network.

Speaking at a news conference for television writers previewing the network's fall lineup, Tarses said she is deeply committed and "very, very excited" about her work at the network and her efforts to improve ABC's ratings.
"It's what gets me out of bed every morning -- the prospect of ultimately getting our network back to No. 1," Tarses said.

Tarses' tenure at the No. 3 network has been the subject of considerable attention in both New York and Hollywood after ABC hired veteran television executive Stuart Bloomberg as chairman of the Entertainment division over Tarses. The controversy intensified this week after a profile of Tarses in The New York Times Magazine angered top executives at ABC and its parent company Walt Disney Co.
Tarses, 33, joined ABC a little over a year ago from rival network NBC, where she helped launch such successful programmes as "Friends".

Wednesday's news conference focused almost exclusively on the executive drama, with reporters repeatedly asking Tarses and Bloomberg about the New York Times article, sexism in the industry and how they plan to work together.
